summary: A lemma-level application bridge for the remaining real-circle SK₁ obstruction. Import every determinant, stable-range, division-ring, circle-ring and Spin target from the accepted U.1 packet. Transfer a jointly continuous determinant-one matrix homotopy into native SO, isolate its three boundary equations, and compose the existing Spin obstruction. The precise LieGroups layer-9 retraction remains the sole supplier boundary.

nodes.title: Transfer a determinant-one circle homotopy into native SO
nodes.statement: Define T_r(H):I×Circle→SO(Q_N) by T_r(H)(p)=r(⟨H(p),det H(p)=1⟩). It is a bundled jointly continuous map, using the existing SL subtype and the native SO topology.
hypotheses: N is a natural number. Q_N=realCliffordForm N 0; SO(Q_N) has the pinned topology induced by specialOrthogonalToGeneralLinear.
I=[0,1]; Circle is the unit circle in ℂ with basepoint 1. SL_N(ℝ) is the existing determinant-one matrix subtype with its coordinate topology.
H:I×Circle→M_N(ℝ) is jointly continuous and det H(p)=1 for every p. r:SL_N(ℝ)→SO(Q_N) is continuous.
proofSteps: Regard p↦⟨H(p),det H(p)=1⟩ as a map to Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup. Continuous.subtype_mk proves joint continuity; no separate continuity in t and z is substituted.
Compose that bundled map with r using ContinuousMap.comp. No homomorphism, smoothness, compactness or homotopy equivalence property of r is used.
For the diagonal non-example test, native special orthogonality preserves Q₂. The coordinate formula and realCliffordForm_apply give Q₂(2e₀)=4 while Q₂(e₀)=1.
acceptance: The construction accepts arbitrary continuous maps r; the identity and fixing conditions are added only to the API lemmas that use them.
The diagonal test distinguishes the native SO carrier from a second copy of the SL subtype.

nodes.title: The transfer fixes each final SO value
nodes.statement: If r fixes native SO coordinate matrices and coord(g)=H(1,z), then T_r(H)(1,z)=g.
hypotheses: N is a natural number. Q_N=realCliffordForm N 0; SO(Q_N) has the pinned topology induced by specialOrthogonalToGeneralLinear.
I=[0,1]; Circle is the unit circle in ℂ with basepoint 1. SL_N(ℝ) is the existing determinant-one matrix subtype with its coordinate topology.
H:I×Circle→M_N(ℝ) is jointly continuous and det H(p)=1 for every p. r:SL_N(ℝ)→SO(Q_N) is continuous.
For every a∈SL_N(ℝ) and g∈SO(Q_N), coord(g)=the underlying matrix of a implies r(a)=g.
z∈Circle and g∈SO(Q_N) satisfy coord(g)=H(1,z).
proofSteps: Use so-homotopy-transfer-apply at (1,z). Its SL argument has coordinate matrix H(1,z), by coe_mk.
Apply the precise coordinate-fixing hypothesis to this SL element and g. No continuous family of SO witnesses is required.
acceptance: The conclusion is equality in the native SO carrier, so applying its coordinate representation gives the exact desired final matrix.

nodes.title: No based SL contraction of the stabilized circle rotation
nodes.statement: Let N≥2 and B_N(z) be the circleEval image of stabilise(2≤N,circleRotation), with upper-left rows (Re z,−Im z),(Im z,Re z) and identity on the complement. Given the continuous native SO retraction in the supplier contract, there is no jointly continuous H:I×Circle→M_N(ℝ) with det H=1, H(0,z)=1, H(1,z)=B_N(z), and H(t,1)=1.
hypotheses: N is a natural number. Q_N=realCliffordForm N 0; SO(Q_N) has the pinned topology induced by specialOrthogonalToGeneralLinear.
I=[0,1]; Circle is the unit circle in ℂ with basepoint 1. SL_N(ℝ) is the existing determinant-one matrix subtype with its coordinate topology.
N≥2; r satisfies the exact native carrier, continuity, identity and coordinate-fixing conditions requested from LieGroups layer 9.
proofSteps: Assume such H exists and form T_r(H) by so-homotopy-transfer. The zero and basepoint API lemmas give the initial identity and the fixed basepoint line.

For each z use Circle.exp_surjective to choose φ with z=Circle.exp φ. Put θ=φ/2. The imported circle-spin-coordinates supplies a native SO element g whose coordinate matrix is B_N(z). This is a pointwise choice only; the already bundled T_r(H) provides continuity.
The one API lemma gives T_r(H)(1,z)=g, hence its coordinate matrix is B_N(z). Apply the imported circle-no-so-contraction to the resulting three boundary equations.

In the imported SK1-real-circle-nonzero proof, combine this theorem with circle-trivial-class-based-contraction. Retain that parent target and its id; no duplicate nontriviality theorem is introduced.
acceptance: The argument applies to every stabilization rank N≥2, including N=2; it uses the parent double-cover endpoint obstruction, not a computation of π₁(SO_N).

In the suggested signature, B_N and the two imported parent outputs are explicit mathematical parameters. Specialization uses circle-spin-coordinates and circle-no-so-contraction exactly as listed here.
The consequent ring statement is nontriviality of the displayed SK₁ class and noninjectivity of the canonical determinant, not a computation of the entire SK₁ group.

sources.match: Positive-diagonal KAN gives a unique analytic K-factor. For an SO input the factors are (g,1,1), so uniqueness fixes it. This supports the precise supplier request; the proof and native topology comparison remain owned by LieGroups layer 9.

targetRefinements.detail: Refine its SL-to-SO application step with the new transfer construction and three boundary lemmas. Retain the parent target id, its algebraic kernel argument and its separate Dedekind prerequisite; assembly should add this theorem to that target’s proof prerequisites.

requests.need: For each N≥2 let Q_N=TauCeti.realCliffordForm N 0. Supply r_N:SL_N(ℝ)→SO(Q_N), continuous from the coordinate topology on Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup into the pinned topology induced by specialOrthogonalToGeneralLinear, with r_N(1)=1. For every a∈SL_N(ℝ) and g∈SO(Q_N), if the faithful coordinate matrix of g equals the underlying matrix of a, require r_N(a)=g. The classical source is the K-factor projection of the unique positive-diagonal KAN decomposition. A supplier stated in matrix SO must include a public continuous comparison into the native quadratic-form SO with this exact coordinate equation. A bare algebraic factorization or a nonunique KAK factor does not meet the contract.

coverage.note: All U.3 targets are retained by reference to the parent packet. The application bridge is decomposed here into six declarations; no parent node or existing planet is duplicated.
remaining: Discharge the single LieGroups layer-9 contract for every N≥2, including the public native-SO topology and coordinate comparison. Replace this stage prerequisite by the supplied declaration or exact supplier node; the parent nontriviality target then uses the six-node application bridge.

gaps.title: Native continuous SO retraction supplied by LieGroups layer 9
gaps.detail: The pinned trees contain neither the required retraction nor a public analytic K-factor API. Morris §7.1 establishes the classical statement, and LieGroups layer 9 explicitly owns its construction. The native SO topology is public, but the matrix-to-native comparison used inside RealSpecialOrthogonal.lean is private. The request specifies both the continuous native result and its coordinate equation; this packet does not claim that the request has been supplied.

planetPolicy: U.1 already assigns six U.3 planets: stable determinant, SK₁, units splitting, semilocal vanishing, Dieudonné determinant and division-ring K₁. This application bridge adds no planet and preserves that stage total.

checked.note: The bundled composite uses the existing determinant-one subtype and induced native SO topology. Its five API items and three distinguishing tests are sufficient; no retraction is constructed here.
Evaluation follows from bundled composition and the subtype constructor; determinant proof arguments do not change the underlying matrix.
The initial boundary follows by subtype extensionality from H(0,z)=1 and then r(1)=1.
The final boundary uses exactly the coordinate-fixing hypothesis on r and the pointwise native SO witness; it requires no continuous angle choice.
The based boundary follows by subtype extensionality from H(t,1)=1 and then r(1)=1.

The transferred continuous homotopy has all three boundaries of the imported SO obstruction. Circle.exp_surjective and the parent half-angle coordinate formula supply each final-boundary witness. The remaining LieGroups retraction is explicitly requested and recorded as a gap.
